column2: pots-findings | fatigue | long_COVID | disease-state | up
column11: A systematic review of 50 controlled studies with over 14 million participants found a 58% increased risk of fatigue following COVID-19.
column12: A systematic review of 50 controlled studies (14 + million participants) found 58% increased fatigue risk following COVID-19 [50].
column13: 58% increased fatigue risk; 50 studies; 14+ million participants

column2: pots-findings | interleukin-6 | long_COVID | disease-state | up
column11: After sensitivity analyses, interleukin-6 levels were significantly higher in PCS cases than in non-PCS cases.
column12: After sensitivity analyses, lymphocytes (SMD = 0.30; 95% CI: 0.12-0.48) and interleukin-6 (SMD = 0.30; 95% CI: 0.12-0.49) were also significantly higher in PCS than non-PCS cases.

column2: eds-findings | joint hypermobility | hypermobility_unspecified | disease-state | up
column11: Pooled analysis of 14 studies found that joint hypermobility was significantly associated with more than double the odds of pelvic organ prolapse.
column12: Overall pooled odds ratio (OR) was 2.37 [95 % confidence interval (CI) 1.54-3.64, I(2) = 77.0 %].

column2: pots-findings | Tryptase | MCAS | disease-state | up
column11: Patients presenting with symptoms related to mast cell activation had numerically higher serum tryptase levels at both baseline and 45-60 minutes post-TILT-table test compared to patients without such symptoms, though this did not reach statistical significance.
column12: Interestingly, serum tryptase levels (both baseline [3.19 ± 1.37 ng/ml vs. 2.99 ± 1.18 ng/ml] and after 45–60 min of the TILT-table test [3.32 ± 1.38 ng/ml vs. 2.799 ± 1.12 ng/ ml]) were higher in patients presenting with symptoms related to MCA compared to others. However, these differences did not reach statistical significance.
column13: Baseline: 3.19±1.37 ng/ml (MCA symptoms) vs 2.99±1.18 ng/ml (no symptoms); post-TILT: 3.32±1.38 ng/ml vs 2.799±1.12 ng/ml

column2: pots-findings | Heart rate variability | dysautonomia | disease-state | down
column11: Prior meta-analytic evidence cited in this review indicates that heart rate variability is reduced in Parkinson's disease patients compared to healthy controls, even at early disease stages.
column12: There is meta-analytic evidence that HRV is lower in patients with PD as compared to healthy controls even at an early stage of the disease [26, 27].

column2: pots-findings | Orthostatic hypotension | dysautonomia | disease-state | up
column11: Across 6 pooled longitudinal studies, baseline orthostatic hypotension was associated with a 27% greater risk of incident dementia.
column12: iii) HR (95 % CI) = 1.267 (1.156; 1.388), P < 0.0001, indicating a 27 % greater risk of incident dementia for those with OH at baseline.

column2: pots-findings | C-reactive protein | long_COVID | disease-state | up
column11: Pooled analysis found elevated C-reactive protein in 8% of post-COVID-19 patients.
column12: C-reactive protein (CRP) (8%, 95% CI 5–12)

column2: eds-findings | type III collagen | EDS_other_type | disease-state | down
column11: The reduction in bone volume fraction (BV/TV) in Col3(+/-) female mice persisted at 1 year of age.
column12: The reduction in BV/TV persisted in female mice at 1 year of age.

column2: pots-findings | Mast cells | MCAS | disease-state | up
column11: Ileal mast cell numbers showed a non-significant tendency to increase (30%) at 12 hours of heat stress compared to thermoneutral controls.
column12: However, regardless of therapeutic treatment, post hoc analysis indicates a tendency for increased (30%) mast cell numbers at 12 h after HS initiation compared to TN controls (P = 0.10; data not shown).

column2: pots-findings | intraepidermal nerve fiber density | small_fiber_neuropathy | disease-state | down
column11: Across anatomical regions, neuropathic patients showed an overall IENFD reduction of about 8.0 fibers/mm compared to healthy individuals, with similar patterns across regions.
column12: Differences across anatomical regions were similar in both groups (interaction p-value = 0.084), with the overall difference between neuropathic patients and healthy individuals being −8.0 (95% CI: −9.2, −6.8; p < 0.001) fibers/mm.

column2: pots-findings | female sex | long_COVID | disease-state | up
column11: Female gender was a consistently documented risk factor for developing long COVID.
column12: The reason for female gender predilection for long COVID has been postulated to be their hormonal influence, excessive inflammatory response, and stronger production of immunoglobulin G (IgG) antibodies activated by the virus24,25.

column2: pots-findings | D-dimer | long_COVID | disease-state | up
column11: D-dimer was reported elevated in 20% of COVID-19 patients during long-term follow-up.
column12: Markers reported to be elevated were D-dimer (20%, 95% CI 6–39), NT-proBNP (11%, 95% CI 6–17) C-reactive protein (8%, 95% CI 5–12), serum ferritin (8% 95% CI 4–14), procalcitonin (4% 95% CI 2–9) and IL-6 (3% 95% CI% 1–7) (Table 2, Figure 2).

column2: pots-findings | fibromyalgia | fibromyalgia | disease-state | up
column11: Fibromyalgia was seen in 21.6% of POTS patients across 5 studies.
column12: Additionally, depression was reported in 34.4% of patients (95% CI: 19.0–54.0, 4 studies, n = 388, Figure S19), while fibromyalgia was seen in 21.6% (95% CI: 12.8–34.2, 5 studies, n = 4532, Figure S21).

column2: pots-findings | Histamine | MCAS | disease-state | up
column11: Plasma histamine levels were significantly higher in allergy-associated ACS patients than in non-allergic ACS patients.
column12: Plasma histamine levels were also higher in the ACS-AL group than in the ACS-NA group (11.4 ± 8.7 vs. 5.6 ± 3.2 ng/mL, P < 0.01; Fig. 2b).

column2: pots-findings | norepinephrine | POTS | disease-state | up
column11: Heart rate increase upon standing correlated with plasma norepinephrine levels after HSCT, supporting a hyperadrenergic phenotype similar to POTS.
column12: The observed correlation between heart rate increase and norepinephrine levels post-HSCT supports a hyperadrenergic phenotype, consistent with existing models of postural orthostatic tachycardia syndrome (POTS).

column2: eds-findings | Beighton score | hypermobility_unspecified | disease-state | up
column11: A Beighton score of 6 or more at age 14 years predicts general pain at age 18 years.
column12: Recent studies have shown that a Beighton score of ≥6 at the age of 10 years is a predictor for pain recurrence and persistence at 14 years,64–66 and a Beighton score of ≥6 at the age of 14 years is a predictor for general pain at 18 years of age.67

column2: eds-findings | generalized joint hypermobility | hypermobility_unspecified | disease-state | up
column11: Women with GJH had significantly higher odds of reporting pelvic girdle pain (PGP) over the entire pregnancy compared with women without GJH, even after adjustment for age and ethnicity.
column12: The association between GJH and PGP for the entire pregnancy remained after adjustment for age and ethnicity (aOR 1.27: 95% CI 1.11–1.47).

column2: pots-findings | Heart rate | dysautonomia | disease-state | up
column11: Supine and upright heart rate increased after bedrest in all groups, but a significant interaction (partial attenuation) was detected only in the supine position, suggesting partial preservation of cardiac autonomic control by cycling and seated interventions.
column12: Supine and upright heart rate increased after bedrest. Despite significant bedrest and group effects, an interaction was detected only in the supine position.
column13: Significant bedrest and group effects on heart rate; interaction detected only in supine position; control group showed numerically largest heart rate increase supine and standing

column2: pots-findings | age | long_COVID | disease-state | up
column11: Advancing age was a consistently documented risk factor for developing long COVID.
column12: Overall, advancing age [odds ratio (OR) 1.08, 95% CI: 1.02–1.15], female gender (OR 1.65, 95% CI: 1.41–1.92), current/former smoking status (OR 1.26, 95% CI: 1.04–1.54) and severity of COVID-19 at initial presentation (OR 1.4, 95% CI: 1.02–1.91) have been consistently documented to be risk factors for the development of long COVID23.

column2: pots-findings | norepinephrine | dysautonomia | disease-state | up
column11: Blood norepinephrine levels were positively associated with higher HF (ms2) HRV power in pheochromocytoma patients.
column12: and blood norepinephrine was associated with higher HF ms2 (0.02, 0.003 to 0.03) (Fig. 5).

column2: pots-findings | Heart rate | POTS | disease-state | up
column11: Supine heart rate was higher in untreated and placebo-treated POTS patients than in controls, but became similar to control following administration of either pyridostigmine or digoxin.
column12: HR became similar to control following administration of either pyridostigmine or digoxin while supine.

column2: pots-findings | body mass index | long_COVID | disease-state | up
column11: A meta-analysis of 41 articles (n=860,783) found that female gender, older age, high BMI, and smoking were associated with increased risk of developing post-COVID-19 condition.
column12: A recent systematic review and meta-analysis26 (41 articles, n=8,60,783 patients) reported that female gender (OR 1.56, 95% CI: 1.41–1.73), age (OR 1.21, 95% CI: 1.11–1.33), high body mass index (BMI) (OR 1.15, 95% CI: 1.08–1.23), and smoking (OR 1.1, 95% CI: 1.07–1.13) were associated with an increased risk of developing post-COVID-19 condition (PCC)26.

column2: pots-findings | Epstein-Barr virus | long_COVID | disease-state | up
column11: A cited comparative meta-analysis found that EBV reactivation was associated with significantly higher mortality among hospitalized patients admitted for symptomatic COVID-19.
column12: Manoharan and Ying found in a comparative meta-analysis that EBV reactivation resulted in significantly higher mortality rates among hospitalized patients admitted for symptomatic COVID-19.

column2: pots-findings | migraine | migraine | disease-state | up
column11: Migraine was reported in 35.6% of POTS patients across 10 studies.
column12: This was closely followed by chronic fatigue, observed in 40.9% of patients (95% CI: 21.1–64.2, 5 studies, n = 4668, Figure S15), and migraine, which had a prevalence of 35.6% (95% CI: 27.0–45.2, 10 studies, n = 4669, Figures S17 and S18).

column2: pots-findings | tryptase | MCAS | disease-state | up
column11: Serum tryptase values are elevated in myeloid neoplasms (AML, CML, myeloproliferative neoplasms, MDS, CMML, chronic eosinophilic leukemia) and mast cell diseases, but generally remain stable in lymphoid neoplasms.
column12: TPS values are elevated in myeloid neoplasms (acute myeloid leukemia, chronic myeloid leukemia, myeloproliferative neoplasms, myelodysplastic syndrome, chronic myelomonocytic leukemia, chronic eosinophilic leukemia)[29,30] and MC diseases (SM, cutaneous mastocytosis), and the TPS value is used as a biomarker in the follow-up of these diseases (Table 1)[31]. In lymphoid neoplasms, TPS values generally remain stable[30].
